Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Today offers strong but sharp thermals (peak w* up to 570 ft/min) with thermal ceilings reaching 7600 ft AGL at some sites. A west-southwest flow develops by midday, making west-facing launches (Hallelujah, West McClellan, Duck Hill) favorable for thermal and ridge soaring, while east-facing sites experience off-direction or lee-side winds and become hazardous in the afternoon. Lapse rates are steep (9–10 °C/km) throughout the area — advanced pilot skills are required.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — brief thermal window early afternoon with light variable winds but off-direction for ridge; strong crosswinds (gusts 29 mph) after 14:00 make flying hazardous. Preferred window 12pm–2pm; peak w* 403 ft/min, ceiling ~3900 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (lapse rate 9.2 °C/km, advanced only).
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — ideal west wind direction all day, moderate speeds (peak 18 mph), strong thermals (517 ft/min) and clear skies. Preferred window 11am–6pm (thermal soaring 12:30–5pm, ridge soaring extends into evening); peak w* 517 ft/min, ceiling ~6000 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.0 °C/km, advanced only).
  • Slide Mountain: Marginal — wind direction mostly off (SW) for SE/S launch; best thermals early but wind increases and becomes cross after 14:00. Preferred window 11am–2pm (best thermal window 12–1:30pm with lighter winds); peak w* 423 ft/min, ceiling ~3600 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.0 °C/km).
  • McClellan: Marginal — favorable wind direction in the morning shifts to west and increases (19 mph) in the afternoon; low-level speed shear (6 mph/layer) and borderline rough turbulence (σw 2.0 m/s). Preferred window 11am–2pm (best thermals 12–2pm with lighter winds); peak w* 570 ft/min (best conditions align with ~470 ft/min), ceiling ~5300 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.8 °C/km, advanced only).
  • West McClellan: Favorable — west wind becomes established by midday and stays within preferred range; good thermals (493 ft/min) with moderate speeds (peak 19 mph). Cloud cover 41% may slightly suppress lift but still soarable. Preferred window 12pm–6pm (thermal soaring 1pm–5pm); peak w* 493 ft/min, ceiling ~4500 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.4 °C/km, advanced only).
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal — variable wind directions; good thermals (peak 506 ft/min) but increasing wind (gusts 22 mph) and off-direction for much of the afternoon; low-level speed shear present. Preferred window 12pm–4pm (best thermals 1pm–3pm with lighter winds); peak w* 506 ft/min, ceiling ~6200 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.1 °C/km, advanced only).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal — favorable morning ridge soaring with E winds 8am–11am (light, within preferred), but afternoon strong W cross/lee winds make launch dangerous. Preferred window 8am–11am for ridge soaring (thermals building); peak w* 333 ft/min, ceiling ~1800 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.1 °C/km) develop later.
  • Duck Hill: Favorable — afternoon west winds favorable for W/NW launch; strong thermals (506 ft/min) and good thermal soaring 1pm–5pm; evening ridge soaring possible. Note wind speeds reach 21 mph and low-level shear exists. Preferred window 1pm–7pm (thermal 1pm–5pm, ridge 5pm–7pm); peak w* 506 ft/min, ceiling ~5000 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.7 °C/km, advanced only).
  • Daydreams: Marginal — thermals extremely weak (peak w* 140 ft/min) but SW winds 12–15 mph provide ridge lift from midday through evening. Preferred window 2pm–7pm for ridge soaring (winds 10–15 mph from SW); peak w* negligible, rely on ridge lift. Sharp thermals (8.9 °C/km) but not relevant due to weak activity.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals — Lapse rates of 8.9–10.1 °C/km at all sites demand advanced pilot skills; powerful, rapid-forming thermals may overwhelm intermediate pilots.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence — Afternoon west winds create rotor downwind of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range ridgelines, particularly hazardous for east-facing launches (Kingsbury, Slide, Rainbow Ridge).
  • Low-level speed shear — Hazardous shear ≥5 mph/layer reported at Kingsbury (5 mph), McClellan (6 mph), Peavine (5 mph), Rainbow Ridge (7 mph), and Duck Hill (6 mph). Expect sudden velocity changes and increased stall risk near these layers.
  • Strong afternoon winds — Several sites experience gusts exceeding 20 mph (Kingsbury 29 mph, Peavine 22 mph, others up to 21 mph), which may exceed safe operating limits for some pilots and increase turbulence.
  • Wind direction shifts — Many east-facing sites see wind direction veer from favorable E/SE in the morning to cross/lee W/SW by midday, rendering ridge soaring dangerous or impossible. Pilots must time flights carefully.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.

w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
